bottom_line: Compared with placebo, dabigatran was associated with a dose-dependent increase in major or clinically relevant minor bleeding, with hazard ratio (HR) 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.
implications: In this phase II trial of patients with recent myocardial infarction on dual antiplatelet therapy, adding dabigatran increased major or clinically relevant minor bleeding in a dose-dependent manner (e.g., HR 4.27 [1.86, 9.81] for 150 mg vs placebo). The study also shows reduced coagulation activity as reflected by lower D-dimer at weeks 1 and 4 (about 37% and 45% lower vs placebo), while ischaemic event rates were low with minor numerical differences across groups (e.g., 3.8% placebo vs 3.0% at 110 mg for the composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal MI, or non-haemorrhagic stroke).

major_points.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation randomized trial in recent MI patients largely on dual antiplatelet therapy.
major_points.quote: In this double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial, 1861 patients (99.2% on dual antiplatelet treatment) in 161 centres were enrolled

major_points.text: Patients were randomized to dabigatran 50, 75, 110, or 150 mg twice daily or placebo.
major_points.quote: randomized to twice daily treatment with dabigatran 50 mg (n ¼ 369), 75 mg (n ¼ 368), 110 mg (n ¼ 406), 150 mg (n ¼ 347), or placebo (n ¼ 371).

major_points.text: Primary outcome was the composite of major or clinically relevant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.
major_points.quote: Primary outcome was the composite of major or clinically rel- evant minor bleeding during the 6-month treatment period.

major_points.text: Primary outcome showed a dose-dependent increase in bleeding vs placebo (HRs reported for each dose).
major_points.quote: compared with placebo, a dose-dependent increase with dabigatran, hazard ratio (HR) 1.77 (95% confidence intervals 0.70, 4.50) for 50 mg; HR 2.17 (0.88, 5.31) for 75 mg; HR 3.92 (1.72, 8.95) for 110 mg; and HR 4.27 (1.86, 9.81) for 150 mg.

major_points.text: D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups at weeks 1 and 4 vs placebo.
major_points.quote: Compared with placebo, D-dimer concentrations were reduced in all dabigatran dose groups by an average of 37 and 45% at weeks 1 and 4, respectively (P , 0.001).
